subject: Post-call recap — Healthlytics migration readiness & compatibility
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, Aug 10, 2026 at 3:12 PM PDT
Subject: Post-call recap — Healthlytics migration readiness & compatibility

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please flag anything I misunderstood.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-token spend and unpredictable billing spikes from current OpenAI usage (monthly overages).
- Rate limit-driven queueing on peak business hours impacting critical customer workflows.
- Need for lower and more predictable latency for multi-turn chat (customer support flows).
- Data residency and stronger key management controls for PHI-adjacent datasets.

Current stack notes you confirmed:
- Primary: OpenAI for generation + Anthropic for assistant experiments (both via an API proxy layer).
- Token mix: heavy chat context usage (~60% system/prompt tokens, ~40% user tokens).
- Integration: real-time streaming to frontend; uses function calling patterns for structured actions.

Success criteria (what Healthlytics wants from a migration):
- Functional parity: support streaming, function/tool-calling, and conversational context retention (KV-style cache).
- Performance parity: median generation latency comparable to current endpoints (target: <300ms for typical 1–2 utterance responses).
- Cost target: reduce per-token spend by ~30–50% at current scale (we'll refine with real usage data).
- Compliance: SOC 2 readiness, KMS/HSM integration, and retention controls.

Initial compatibility observations (from our side):
- Redwood supports the streaming and function call patterns you need; we can preserve your proxy layer while routing to open-model backends.
- Shortlist we suggested today for evaluation: Llama 2 70B (quantized line), Mistral 8x (generation efficiency), Falcon 40B-instruct (for instruction-following comparisons). We also mentioned smaller adapter-based models for cost-sensitive tiers.
- Important feature asks you raised: consistent token accounting across model variants, cold-start KV cache behavior, and autoscaling for peak windows.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) You: share a redacted 24‑hour sample of invocation logs (no PII) or a synthetic workload so we can run cost/latency sims.
2) Redwood: run a perf/cost matrix using your sample workload against the three shortlisted models and produce a summary (latency P50/P95, token cost estimate, and quality notes).
3) Commercial: Aditya will prepare a preliminary pricing/POC proposal + mutual action plan.
4) Compliance: Monica will surface the SOC 2/KMS artifacts and outline what we would need for Healthlytics' procurement.

Proposed timeline:
- Perf sims & draft POC plan: by Aug 20.
- Internal review + procurement intro: week of Aug 23.
- Target PoC kickoff: week of Aug 24 (2–3 week evaluation).

Attachments: Migration-Checklist.xlsx (checklist template), Redwood-POC-template.pdf (standard POC scope).

Shared doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcdExampleMigrationPlan

If that looks right I can loop in engineering to reserve a small test harness and get the perf runs scheduled. Thanks again — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123
Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Grant <sophie@healthlytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthlytics.com
Date: Tue, Aug 11, 2026 at 9:20 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Healthlytics migration readiness & compatibility

Thanks Marcus — this is a clean recap, appreciate the clarity. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

Clarifications:
- Token volume: our average monthly token consumption is ~1.1B tokens (mixed prompts + responses). During product events it spikes ~2.5x for 6–10 hours.
- Latency target: 300ms median is fine for a single-turn reply; for multi-turn flows our SLA target is 500ms end-to-end (including frontend streaming assembly).

Security/compliance notes:
- Procurement will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and an outline of KMS integration options (we use AWS KMS, must support customer-managed keys).
- Data retention policy: we keep conversational logs for 90 days; any PII must be deleted on request.

Evaluation ask:
- Can Redwood provide a short (48–72 hour) perf run against an anonymized/synthetic stream before committing to a 2–3 week PoC? That will help us validate rate-limit behavior.

Procurement: procurement@healthlytics.com is on copy — they will follow up on contracting and any non-standard clauses.

If you can get the perf sims and a short smoke run scheduled, we can align internal stakeholders for the Aug 24 target.

— Sophie
Sophie Grant
VP Product — Healthlytics
sophie@healthlytics.com
